text: The Oct. 8 edition reported that the court file in 4FA-24-02136CR recorded no verdict, no remand and no sentencing hearing, and that the conviction was public only through a Department of Law release. The file read on Oct. 9 carries a docket row dated Oct. 2 reading Jury Related Document: Verdicts I and II, a temporary order of commitment pending final judgment of the same date, and a sentencing hearing on March 18, 2027 on its event list. Ten docket rows are new since that reading and all ten carry dates between Sep. 28 and Oct. 2. Whether those rows were entered after the Oct. 8 reading or were present and missed cannot be established from the file, and neither is asserted.

The Oct. 8 edition gave the date of the last docket entry in 4FA-26-01446CR as Oct. 5 and in 4FA-26-01938CR as Oct. 1. Both files were re-read on Oct. 9 under a revised method of counting docket rows, which excludes bail continuation lines, and the last dated entry is Oct. 2 in the first and Sep. 29 in the second. No other case on this list changed its last docket date backwards.

The Oct. 7 edition reported that the court file in 4FA-26-02028CR carried one count recorded as charging document pending or not filed, with no charge class and no docket entry of any kind. The file now carries one count of assault in the third degree, cause fear of injury with a weapon, a Class C felony, and the defendant was arraigned on Oct. 7. The file carried no charge when it was read on the morning of Oct. 7.

The Oct. 7 edition reported that the charge list in 4NE-26-00096CR carried seven counts, among them a second count of burglary in the first degree, in a dwelling, a Class B felony, at Cantwell. The charge list read on Oct. 8 carries six counts and no count carries that tracking number. Nothing on the court file records why, and its most recent docket entry is dated Oct. 6.

The Oct. 7 edition reported that an arraignment was held on Oct. 5 in 4FA-26-02019CR. The court's event list records the arraignments of Oct. 4 and Oct. 5 as continued, and an arraignment held on Oct. 7.

The Oct. 7 edition reported that the Alaska Department of Law had published nothing in six days and that its most recent release was the Oct. 1 Office of Special Prosecutions review. Two releases dated Oct. 5 stand above it on the department's index, one of them the Fairbanks sexual abuse conviction carried in this edition. The two releases did not appear in the reading taken on the morning of Oct. 7.

The Oct. 6 edition reported that no criminal court file existed over the conditions-of-release violation that troopers referred to the District Attorney's Office on Oct. 5. A case was filed at Fairbanks on Oct. 5, 4FA-26-02026CR, carrying two counts, and a warrant was issued on it on Oct. 6. The case did not appear in the court's public database or its weekly report when those were searched on the morning of Oct. 6.

The Oct. 6 edition reported the case judge in 4FA-26-01896CR as Harbison. The case judge field now records no assigned judge, and the omnibus hearing and trial week have moved from Dec. 1 and Dec. 14 to Nov. 5 and Nov. 23.
The Oct. 5 edition reported that the arraignment in 4FA-26-02019CR was held on Oct. 4. The court's event list records that arraignment as continued, with a second arraignment held on Oct. 5.

The Oct. 5 edition reported that neither 4FA-26-02020CR nor 4FA-26-02014CR appeared in any trooper dispatch or police bulletin entry. The Fairbanks Police Department daily bulletin now records an arrest at the 1000 block of Kellum Street at 11:29 p.m. on Oct. 3 on a charge of criminal mischief in the fifth degree, case 26003039, which corresponds to 4FA-26-02020CR. The entry was added to the bulletin after Oct. 5.

The Oct. 4 edition reported that a Fairbanks-area case number filed and closed on Oct. 4 with no charging document, 4FA-26-02018CR, still returned records in Alaska CourtView, and used that to withdraw an earlier explanation for other case numbers that return none. That case number returned No Records Found on Oct. 5, by case number and by name search. The statement that such a case still returns records is withdrawn, and no explanation is now offered for the case numbers that do not resolve.

The Oct. 4 edition reported that no court file existed for the domestic violence arrest made at Healy on Oct. 3. A case was filed at the Nenana court on Oct. 4, 4NE-26-00099CR, carrying three counts, all recorded as domestic violence related.

The Oct. 4 edition reported that the Alaska Court System's weekly criminal charges report did not contain 4FA-26-02014CR, a seventh case filed at Fairbanks on Saturday, Oct. 3. The report run at 9 p.m. on Oct. 4 contains it under that date.

The Oct. 4 morning edition reported six criminal cases filed at Fairbanks on Saturday, Oct. 3, taken from the court's weekly charges report. The court filed seven: 4FA-26-02014CR, carrying two domestic violence counts, has a file date of Oct. 3 and is not contained in that report.

Earlier editions explained the Fairbanks case numbers that return no records in Alaska CourtView by stating that a case closed for want of a charging document does not appear in the public database until charges arrive. A case in that state, 4FA-26-02018CR, was read on Oct. 4 and does return records, by case number and by name, so that explanation is withdrawn as an account of those seven numbers.

The Oct. 4 morning edition carried a compiled time of 05:05 AKDT. The publishing platform timestamps that edition at 03:48 AKDT and this file at 03:58 AKDT, while the edition also records individual readings as late as 04:44. The two cannot both be right and this record cannot establish which clock is wrong; both are kept, and the time given is the time the edition was published.

The Oct. 2 edition said the Alaska Department of Law's press index carried no item about the Office of Special Prosecutions review of the July 7 Fairbanks trooper shooting. The department published that review on its press index, dated Oct. 1, and it states that the review was completed Sept. 29. Whether the item was added after the Oct. 2 reading or was present and missed cannot be established.

The Oct. 2 edition said it had been fifteen days since the Alaska Department of Law announced the outcome of a Fairbanks-area case. Its Oct. 1 release on the trooper shooting review is a Fairbanks-area item, so that run ended on Oct. 1.

The Oct. 2 edition listed four events on the Fairbanks police bulletin for Oct. 1. The page now holds 25, including an aggravated assault with a weapon that appears in no other public record. Counts taken from this feed are minimums and can rise sharply after publication.

The Oct. 1 edition said the two daily public feeds had posted three events in total between Sept. 28 and Oct. 1. The Fairbanks police bulletin has since added an arrest made on Sept. 30, a date that had shown no events on two earlier readings, and listed four events for Oct. 1. Counts taken from these feeds are minimums and can rise after publication.

The Sept. 30 edition gave the judge in the North Pole kidnapping case, 4FA-26-01890CR, as Schwalm. The case judge is Temple; the court file records a change of judge by peremptory disqualification from Judge Schwalm to Judge Temple on Sept. 22.

The Sept. 29 edition reported that the Fairbanks police bulletin showed no events for Sept. 27 and gave counts for Sept. 21 through Sept. 26 as 15, one, eight, five, one and two. The bulletin has since added sixteen events across five of those dates: Sept. 22 now holds two, Sept. 24 six, Sept. 25 seven, Sept. 26 seven and Sept. 27 three, including a robbery with a cutting instrument and an aggravated assault.

The Sept. 29 edition gave Your Alaska Link's newest Interior crime item as a Sept. 23 death. The outlet had published an account of the Sept. 16 Fairbanks narcotics operation on Sept. 25, updated Sept. 28, which was on its crime section at the time of that reading.

An earlier edition published today gave KTVF / WebCenter Fairbanks as carrying nothing from the Fairbanks area since Sept. 18. KTVF published a report on the death of a Fairbanks man pinned by a tractor on Sept. 23 at 12:12 p.m., filed under general news rather than under crime. The outlet's most recent Fairbanks-area item is therefore Sept. 23, not Sept. 18.

Monday's edition listed the most recent docket entry in case 4FA-24-02118CR, against Cedar Mae Sarten, as dated Sept. 9. The docket carries two later entries dated Sept. 25, including the State's sentencing memorandum and Rule 32.1 notice.

Monday's edition reported that three Fairbanks case numbers printed in the court's weekly report returned no record in the public case index. One of the three, 4FA-26-01901CR, now appears in that index with two charges filed, a warrant issued Sept. 28 and a hearing set for Sept. 29. A case number can be closed when no charging document is filed and reopen when charges arrive, at which point it becomes visible; the two court records were not in conflict.

The Sept. 27 edition reported an arrest near Clay Street and Second Avenue on a charge police recorded as a felony assault in the third degree with a weapon. The charge filed in court on Sept. 27 is one count of assault in the fourth degree, a Class A misdemeanor; the court file records no felony count.

The Sept. 27 edition listed five counts in case 4FA-26-01644CR. The case carries six counts; the sixth is violating a condition of release for a felony, a Class A misdemeanor. The public case index displays only five charges per case and holds further counts behind a link.

An earlier version of Monday's edition reported that neither of the weekend's two Fairbanks domestic violence arrests had a court file. Complaints were filed in both on the morning of Sept. 28 and both men were arraigned that afternoon; one file carries two felony counts. The statement was accurate at the time of the morning reading and had ceased to be so by midday.
The Sep. 26 edition listed 11 of the 13 Fairbanks filings for Sep. 25. The two omitted cases, 4FA-26-01922CR and 4FA-26-01926CR (both theft 4), have been added.
Earlier editions stated that no Fourth District grand jury indictment had appeared since Sep. 2. An indictment in 4FA-26-01446CR was returned Sep. 9.
